clusters.label: In-app reference example as composition model
clusters.family: Model on the design system's own in-app example
clusters.definition: The agent wants to see how the design system itself builds the very piece of UI it is about to build or change: which components and props are used, how they are laid out, labelled and wired together in context. An app-context story (named or described after that screen, row or panel) is the vehicle because it is the design system's own rendition of the target, whereas the sibling stories only isolate single props or are tests.
clusters.include: First-time loads of an app-context story, usually listed by name or description without source, to copy its layout, prop choices, emphasis hierarchy, labelling or surrounding markup; also multi-facet questions about the example's overall structure (e.g. form element plus headings plus props) with no single focal mechanism.
clusters.exclude: If the need is a single yes/no mechanism about form submission (is there a real form, a submit button, a submit type) it goes to k02; if it is whether native attributes are passed to the component it goes to k03. If the trigger says this story's source had already been printed and came back thin or as a one-line wrapper, it goes to k17. If the agent loads it after finishing the work to check conformance, k04. If an in-app story of a different component is loaded to learn what that other component is for, k16.

clusters.label: Reference example checked for form/submit wiring
clusters.family: Model on the design system's own in-app example
clusters.definition: The agent has a specific hypothesis about native form semantics (fields need a real form element, some control must act as submit) and wants to know whether the design system's own in-app example embodies that pattern, so it can confirm the diagnosis and copy the wiring. An app-context story is the vehicle because it is the only place a whole form or a real call-to-action, rather than a bare single control, would be shown.
clusters.include: App-context stories loaded to answer 'does the reference wrap its fields in a form, and what submits it?' or 'does the reference show a button that submits (submit type or form wrapper)?', including loads made right after a narrower test story returned only a bare control.
clusters.exclude: General 'how is this example laid out and which props does it use' goes to k01. Questions about non-submit native attributes (name, autocomplete, input type) in the example go to k03. Questions put to a test story named for the default type go to k05; speculative looks into Anatomy or Variants for a submit option go to k06.

clusters.label: Reference example checked for native attributes
clusters.family: Model on the design system's own in-app example
clusters.definition: The props table lists only a couple of design-system props, and the agent wants evidence of whether native HTML attributes (name, type, autocomplete) are passed to the component in practice. The design system's own in-app example is the vehicle because real usage would reveal attributes the props table omits.
clusters.include: App-context stories loaded primarily to see whether native attributes beyond the documented props are passed to the component in the reference usage.
clusters.exclude: If the focal question is the form element or submission, k02. If native attributes are only one facet among layout, grouping and headings, k01. If the same question is put to a structural or sole story (Anatomy) rather than an in-app example, k06; if put to a test story named for the attribute, k05.

clusters.label: Post-build check against the reference
clusters.family: Model on the design system's own in-app example
clusters.definition: The feature is already implemented and passing, and the agent loads the design system's in-app example of the same UI to check that what it just built matches the reference arrangement. The story serves as an acceptance reference rather than as a starting model.
clusters.include: Loads of an in-app reference story made after the implementation is finished, to compare the result with the reference.
clusters.exclude: Any load made before or during implementation to obtain a model goes to k01 (or k02/k03 for targeted checks).

clusters.label: Test story asserting undocumented native contract
clusters.family: Verify a specific behaviour or contract
clusters.definition: The agent needs one precise fact about how the component treats the underlying native element that the props table does not state: a hard-coded attribute default, whether a caller can override it, whether refs and native props are forwarded. A test-style story whose name literally states that contract is the vehicle, because its name promises a direct, authoritative answer where the docs are silent.
clusters.include: First-time loads of a story named for a native-attribute default or for ref/prop forwarding, triggered by that attribute or capability being absent from the props table (e.g. default button type and whether it can submit; forwarding of ref, id, tabIndex).
clusters.exclude: If the story's full source had already been printed in a docs dump and it is re-loaded on its own, k18. If the same question is put to a story not named for the attribute (Anatomy, Variants, Class Name, a sole story), k06. If it is put to an in-app example, k02 or k03. Stories named for accessibility behaviour (announcements, reported range) go to k09; stories named for limits behaviour go to k08.

clusters.label: Indirect probe for element or attribute support
clusters.family: Verify a specific behaviour or contract
clusters.definition: The agent still wants to know what element the component renders and whether native attributes or a submit capability can reach it, but no story is named for that fact (or the direct one has been exhausted). It therefore opens a general-purpose story (Anatomy, Variants, Class Name, the only story left unread, the only story the component has) as a speculative probe, on the reasoning that structure or pass-through shown there might reveal the answer.
clusters.include: Anatomy, Variants, Class Name, last-unseen or sole stories loaded to look for the rendered element, a type/submit option, or acceptance of native attributes such as autocomplete, name or type; the story is a proxy, not named for the fact sought.
clusters.exclude: A story literally named for the attribute or contract goes to k05. Anatomy loaded to learn parts and how to use the component goes to k10 or k11. Variants loaded to find visual styles goes to k13. Class Name loaded to restyle the component goes to k07.

clusters.label: className story as styling escape hatch
clusters.family: Verify a specific behaviour or contract
clusters.definition: The agent needs to know whether the component can be restyled or positioned from outside because the built-in variants do not cover the look it needs. The story dedicated to the className prop is the vehicle because it documents the customisation hook.
clusters.include: Class Name stories loaded to confirm custom classes (and similar extras) are accepted so the agent can colour, style or position the component.
clusters.exclude: Class Name loaded as proxy evidence that arbitrary native attributes pass through (not for styling) goes to k06. Looking for built-in visual variants goes to k13.

clusters.label: Behaviour rule at value bounds
clusters.family: Verify a specific behaviour or contract
clusters.definition: The agent wants the component's runtime rule at the edges of its range: whether controls disable, clamp or wrap at min and max, and whether a given value can be reached. A story named for that boundary behaviour is the vehicle because it describes a behavioural rule that plain prop demos and the props table defaults do not convey.
clusters.include: Stories whose name states behaviour at limits, loaded to learn edge behaviour and judge whether it suits the intended use.
clusters.exclude: Stories named after a single bound prop and loaded just to see how to set it would be k10. Anatomy loaded for general structure goes to k11. Test stories about what is reported to assistive technology go to k09.

clusters.label: Built-in assistive-technology semantics
clusters.family: Verify a specific behaviour or contract
clusters.definition: The agent needs to know what the component itself exposes or announces to assistive technology without extra work: how an error is announced, whether the message node is always mounted, what range and name a progress element reports. A test-style story named for exactly that accessibility behaviour is the vehicle, because it asserts semantics that are invisible in the props table.
clusters.include: Stories named for an announcement, an always-mounted slot or a reported range, loaded to learn the component's own ARIA and live-region behaviour.
clusters.exclude: What the caller should pass as an accessible name or label goes to k12. Anatomy loaded for parts where ARIA is one item among several goes to k10 or k11. In-app examples loaded to see how a status is conveyed in context go to k01.

clusters.label: Baseline usage of a component being adopted
clusters.family: Learn how to use or configure a component
clusters.definition: The agent is about to use a component in new UI and needs its basic operating model: which props drive it, what element or parts it consists of, what slots or options it offers. A structural or implementation-named story (Anatomy, Native Control, or the single story the docs offer) is the vehicle as the first available worked example of the component on its own.
clusters.include: First-line loads of Anatomy or similar stories to learn props, parts, slots, ARIA exposure and state wiring before writing new usage of the component.
clusters.exclude: If Anatomy is opened as a fallback because an example story just came back opaque or uninformative, k11. If opened to find native attributes or a submit option, k06. If the story name was guessed rather than listed, k14. If the story had already been seen and is re-loaded for more, k17. If the aim is when-to-use guidance, k15.

clusters.label: Anatomy as fallback after uninformative example
clusters.family: Learn how to use or configure a component
clusters.definition: A more promising story (typically the in-app example) has just returned an opaque helper or only trivial usage, and written guidance is missing, so the agent still lacks a concrete picture of the component's parts and how it is meant to be operated or composed. The Anatomy story is the vehicle because, among the remaining unseen stories, it is the one that promises a structural breakdown rather than a single prop, bound or test.
clusters.include: Anatomy loads explicitly triggered by an earlier story being a one-line wrapper or uninformative, seeking parts, intended interaction, wiring of value/handlers/labels, or internal accessibility wiring; includes cases where the structure is wanted in order to weigh the component against an alternative.
clusters.exclude: Anatomy as a first look with no failed predecessor goes to k10. Anatomy probed for native attributes or type goes to k06. Re-loading the opaque story itself goes to k17. A sole story mined for when-to-use guidance goes to k15.

clusters.label: How to name the control accessibly
clusters.family: Learn how to use or configure a component
clusters.definition: The agent needs to know what accessible name the caller must supply and how: which prop carries it, whether it renders visibly or only names the element, and what wording the design system uses. A story dedicated to the label/aria-label prop or to a labelling rule is the vehicle, because it is the one place an example of the intended name is shown.
clusters.include: Stories named for an aria-label or label prop, or for a rule such as icon-only controls needing a label, loaded to learn mechanism and expected wording of the accessible name.
clusters.exclude: What the component announces or reports by itself goes to k09. In-app examples loaded to see labelling in context go to k01.

clusters.label: Catalogue of visual variants
clusters.family: Learn how to use or configure a component
clusters.definition: The task calls for distinct visual emphases (primary versus secondary) but the props table shows only a few boolean flags and no variant prop. The agent loads the catalogue story that shows all styles side by side to learn which looks exist and which props select them.
clusters.include: Variants-type stories loaded to survey available styles and map them to props for a visual hierarchy need.
clusters.exclude: In-app examples loaded to see how primary and secondary actions are paired in the real panel go to k01. Variants scanned for a non-visual capability such as a submit option goes to k06. Class Name for custom styling goes to k07.

clusters.label: Guessed story name for a state
clusters.family: Learn how to use or configure a component
clusters.definition: The docs offered almost nothing, so the agent requests a story it was never shown, guessing a conventional name for the state it needs to understand (how the component is opened and closed). The vehicle is an assumed naming convention rather than a listed story.
clusters.include: Loads of a story id that no docs output had listed, chosen by convention to learn state wiring.
clusters.exclude: Loads of a listed structural story for the same purpose go to k10.

clusters.label: Sole story mined for usage guidance
clusters.family: Decide which component fits the job
clusters.definition: The agent is trying to establish when or where a component should be used (versus alternatives) and has found no guidance pages, MDX or descriptions. It loads the component's only story as the last remaining documented source, hoping the story-level view carries a description or usage hint that the terse component page lacked.
clusters.include: Loads of a component's single story (Empty, Anatomy) made after guideline searches failed, with the stated aim of finding usage or when-to-use guidance rather than markup.
clusters.exclude: A sole story loaded to see what its wrapper renders or as a usage model goes to k17 (already shown) or k10 (first look). A sole story probed for native attributes goes to k06. Anatomy chosen among several stories after an opaque example goes to k11.

clusters.label: Rival component's in-app role
clusters.family: Decide which component fits the job
clusters.definition: The app uses one component for a job that another component may be meant for, and the agent wants to know what the design system actually uses the incumbent component for. The incumbent's own in-app story is the vehicle because it shows the component's intended role, by contrast with the misuse in the app.
clusters.include: In-app stories of the alternative or incumbent component loaded to learn its intended purpose and contrast it with the use under question.
clusters.exclude: In-app stories of the component the agent intends to use, loaded as a model, go to k01.

clusters.label: Re-load thin or wrapper-only story
clusters.family: Second look at an already-printed story
clusters.definition: The agent has already been shown this story (in a full docs dump or an earlier view), but what it saw was a one-line helper or wrapper call or otherwise too thin to act on. It loads the story individually hoping the single-story view exposes the markup, composition or call hidden behind the helper.
clusters.include: Re-loads where the trigger says the story's source was already printed or seen and the need is what the helper actually renders or does, or a fuller version of the same example; covers in-app wrappers and generic demo helpers alike.
clusters.exclude: First-time loads of an example listed only by name or description go to k01. Re-loading an already-printed test story to pin down one fact goes to k18. Turning to a different story (Anatomy) after the wrapper disappointed goes to k11. An already-shown sole story loaded to hunt for when-to-use guidance rather than markup goes to k15.

clusters.label: Re-load printed test story in isolation
clusters.family: Second look at an already-printed story
clusters.definition: The component docs came back as a long dump of every story with no props table, so the fact the agent needs (a native-attribute default) was technically already on screen inside a test story. The agent loads that one story by itself to isolate and re-read it, or in case the single view says more.
clusters.include: Individual loads of a named test story whose source the trigger says was already printed in the full docs output.
clusters.exclude: First-time loads of the same kind of test story from a names-only list go to k05. Re-loads of wrapper or example stories for hidden markup go to k17.
